gaps.sentence: The village ___ my grandmother was born has no shops.
gaps.explanation: 'Where' is the relative adverb for places; 'which' cannot stand alone here because no preposition is present.

gaps.sentence: All ___ I want is a quiet weekend at home.
gaps.explanation: After 'all' the relative pronoun is 'that' (often omitted); 'all what' is always wrong.

gaps.sentence: The candidate ___ speech impressed us most got the job.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose speech' — the speech belonged to the candidate.

gaps.sentence: The reason ___ the flight was diverted has never been made public.
gaps.explanation: 'The reason why' — 'why' is the relative for reasons.

gaps.sentence: It was the first time ___ I had ever driven on my own.
gaps.hint: after 'the first time', use this pronoun
gaps.explanation: 'The first time that ...' is the standard pattern; the pronoun may also be omitted, but 'which' and 'what' do not fit.

gaps.sentence: The hotel, ___ rates include breakfast, is fully booked for the conference.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose' marks possession even for things: the hotel whose rates…

gaps.sentence: We must decide ___ to do next.
gaps.explanation: 'What to do' is the standard pattern meaning 'the thing that we should do'.

gaps.sentence: The children were amazed by ___ they saw at the circus.
gaps.explanation: 'What they saw' means 'the things that they saw'; after the preposition 'by' only a nominal clause like this fits.
